name: KKr DUP, Emotional-Level, and XML-Armed Doctrine
purpose: Govern how KKr handles duplicate or near-duplicate KKs across many sources while preserving depth, emotional levels, and future XML-ready interchange.
core_law: DUPs are allowed when they improve selection depth, emotional-level coverage, or future review quality. DUPs must not create public confusion.

dup_rules.A_best_one_wins_when_same: When two candidates are meaningfully the same, the best reviewed candidate wins.
dup_rules.B_if_tie_no_change: If two same-level candidates tie, no forced change is required. Keep both internally or hold until stronger evidence appears.
dup_rules.C_emotional_levels_convene: Duplicate or similar candidates may remain valuable when they serve different emotional levels, relationship contexts, sensory profiles, or use-case depths.

emotional_level_requirement.depth_law: Do not collapse meaningful emotional levels into a single flat tag.
emotional_level_requirement.buyer_safety_law: Only approved_public records may reach buyer-facing routes.

xml_armed_requirement.meaning: A record is XML-armed when it can be serialized into a stable future XML exchange envelope without losing source, review, safety, emotional-level, or routing meaning.
xml_armed_requirement.xml_public_guard: XML readiness does not equal public approval.

not_allowed: Do not expose DUP logic in public buyer copy.
Do not publish tied candidates merely because they exist.
Do not let raw inventory become buyer-facing.
Do not let XML-ready records bypass human review.
Do not let mKs enter current K-KUT buyer flow through this doctrine.
locked_summary: KKr may retain DUPs for depth. Best wins when same. Ties may remain internal. Emotional levels must convene. Records should be XML-armed before wider system propagation.
